artifacts_in: docs/requirements.yaml (REQ-029 entry, and REQ-028/REQ-030 for context)

task.description: Design the extension to lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex for REQ-029: validate_node_attributes/1 (PD-05 per-node-type required-attribute rules) and the edge-condition rules (PD-06) folded into validate_graph/1 or a sibling function, plus isValidCelSyntax's minimal structural CEL check. Branch feature/WF02-REQ029-20260817 already exists and is checked out. Must explicitly confirm or override REQ-028's design doc section 9.1 (Node.attributes typing: map() | nil vs raw JSON string) rather than silently inheriting it -- REQ-028's own design flagged this exact question for REQ-029 to resolve. Also state explicitly which function/module owns the edge-condition checks (definition.md gives no separate function name beyond 'the validateGraph() extension') per REQ-029's own text.
acceptance_criteria: each of the 7 node types has at least one explicit test: HUMAN_TASK missing role, SERVICE_TASK missing endpoint, SERVICE_TASK invalid timeout (0 and >300000), TIMER missing/invalid duration, TIMER P0D explicitly accepted, and START/END/gateway types accepting no attributes
an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge with both a non-null condition and is_default: true is rejected
an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY with two edges both marked is_default: true is rejected
isValidCelSyntax-equivalent rejects at least one structurally invalid expression and accepts at least one structurally valid one, with an explicit test noting it performs no evaluation
extra undeclared attributes on a node do not cause a violation, demonstrated by an explicit test

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req029-node-attribute-edge-condition-validators.md, extending REQ-028's Letflow.Definitions.Graph (lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex) with two new sibling public functions -- validate_node_attributes/1 (PD-05, CHK-09..CHK-12: HUMAN_TASK role, SERVICE_TASK endpoint+timeout_ms range, TIMER duration_iso8601) and validate_edge_conditions/1 (PD-06, CHK-13..CHK-17: gateway condition presence/absence, default+condition conflict, at-most-one-default-per-gateway, CEL syntax) -- plus a new public valid_cel_syntax?/1 minimal structural (no-evaluation) CEL check. Decided and documented explicitly: PD-06 gets its own sibling function rather than folding into validate_graph/1 (which is already merged/gate-approved and has no notion of conditional ordering), flagged that REQ-030's current text only names validateNodeAttributes() so its CODE-DESIGNER must also call validate_edge_conditions/1; ordering ('run only after validate_graph/1 passes') is caller-enforced (REQ-030's future create/1), not enforced inside this module -- both new functions are total/defensive and never call validate_graph/1 themselves. Resolved REQ-028 design doc section 9.1 explicitly: Node.attributes stays map() | nil, with a new pinned sub-decision that keys must be String.t() (not atoms, to avoid atom-table exhaustion from decoding untrusted JSON keys) and the exact key names/value types each check reads. R-Co's graph.zig/definition.md source was not reachable in this environment (searched the filesystem, no R-Co checkout present) -- the ISO-8601 duration scan-forward parser (section 4.3) and the CEL syntax algorithm (section 6) are therefore reconstructed from REQ-029's own requirement text rather than verified against source, and this gap is flagged explicitly in the design doc's section 0 and section 9.1 rather than presented as a verified port. All 5 acceptance criteria are mapped to concrete design elements in the doc's section 11 traceability table. No implementation code written -- signatures, type shapes, and prose algorithm steps only.
